question: Is this the smallest version that still works?
summary: Reviews work for complexity that is not earning its place, and proposes the smallest version that still meets the goal.
share: Is this the smallest version that still works? Reviews AI work for complexity that is not earning its place.
homeBlurb: Look for complexity that does not earn its place.
tryOnce: Review the current work using a keep-it-simple pass. Point out complexity that is not earning its place — unnecessary abstraction, indirection, structure or process — and describe the smallest version that still meets the goal, including what it gives up. Preserve anything justified by a real constraint and name that constraint. If the current complexity is warranted, say so plainly rather than simplifying for its own sake.

example.caption: A simple implementation has accumulated unnecessary abstractions.

turns.text: I added one field to the settings form and it's touched 14 files.
The field goes through a FieldRegistry, a validator factory and a config schema, so new fields are declarative.

That structure would earn its place at thirty fields. There are four. Keep the config schema — the API already reads it. The rest can collapse into the input, one validation check beside it, and the existing save call. Three files instead of fourteen.

usefulWhen: A small change has spread across many files.
New abstractions appeared that the goal did not ask for.
Something is hard to explain, or hard to change safely.
notNeededWhen: The complexity is load-bearing and you already know why.
The work is genuinely intricate and the structure reflects that.
Simplifying now would cost more than living with it.

choices.label: Gentle
choices.line: - **Simplification pressure.** Flag only complexity that is actively causing a problem now — something hard to change, hard to explain, or already a source of bugs.

choices.label: Balanced
choices.line: - **Simplification pressure.** Flag complexity that is not currently carrying weight, but leave anything with a plausible near-term justification in place.

choices.label: Aggressive
choices.line: - **Simplification pressure.** Flag every piece of structure that is not currently required, and default to removing it unless a present constraint demands otherwise.

options.label: Tolerance for abstraction
options.help: When an abstraction counts as speculative.

choices.label: Tolerant
choices.line: - **Abstractions.** Accept an abstraction with a single caller where it genuinely makes the code clearer, and question only those with no caller or no clear purpose.

choices.label: Balanced
choices.line: - **Abstractions.** Treat an abstraction with a single caller as speculative unless a second use is already known and imminent.

choices.label: Strict
choices.line: - **Abstractions.** Treat every abstraction as speculative until a second real use exists, however much clearer it appears.

options.label: Scope of review
options.help: Whether surrounding architecture is in scope.

choices.label: Changed work only
choices.line: - **Scope of review.** Review only the work that has recently changed. Leave surrounding architecture out of the discussion entirely.

choices.label: Changed work, plus its causes
choices.line: - **Scope of review.** Review the work that has recently changed, and mention surrounding architecture only where it is the direct cause of the complexity.

choices.label: Include surrounding architecture
choices.line: - **Scope of review.** Review the changed work together with the surrounding architecture, including structure that predates this task.

options.label: Prose and responses
options.help: Whether the same lens applies to writing.

choices.label: Code only
choices.line: - **Prose and responses.** Review code and structure only; leave the wording of explanations and responses alone.

choices.label: Code and writing
choices.line: - **Prose and responses.** Review the complexity of explanations and responses as well as code — over-long answers, unnecessary caveats, and restated context.
